Wellness and Healthy Decisions: Health
A state of complete physical, mental, and social wellbeing
Wellness
The active pursuit of choices that support overall health
Dimensions of wellness
Physical, mental, emotional, social, and environmental health
Risk behavior
An action that increases the chance of harm or illness
Protective factor
A condition that reduces the likelihood of harm
Decision-making model
A stepwise process of identifying options and weighing consequences
Refusal skills
Techniques for declining pressure without damaging relationships
Peer pressure
Influence from people of similar age to act a certain way
Goal setting
Defining specific, measurable outcomes with a timeline
Short-term versus long-term goal
An outcome within weeks versus one taking months or years
Health literacy
The ability to find and use reliable health information
Preventive care
Screenings and checkups aimed at catching problems early
Nutrition: Nutrient
A substance in food the body uses for energy, growth, or repair
Macronutrient
Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats, needed in large amounts
Micronutrient
Vitamins and minerals, needed in small amounts
Carbohydrate
The body's primary energy source, at four calories per gram
Complex carbohydrate
Starches and fibre that digest slowly and sustain energy
Protein
A nutrient supplying amino acids for tissue building and repair
Complete protein
A protein containing all nine essential amino acids
Saturated fat
A fat solid at room temperature that raises LDL cholesterol
Unsaturated fat
A liquid fat from plants and fish that supports heart health
Trans fat
An industrially processed fat linked to cardiovascular disease
Dietary fiber
Indigestible plant material supporting digestion and satiety
Calorie
A unit measuring the energy food provides
Energy balance
The relationship between calories consumed and calories expended
Nutrition Facts label
The panel listing serving size, calories, and nutrient amounts
Percent Daily Value
How much a serving contributes to a 2,000-calorie reference diet
Hydration
Maintaining adequate body water for temperature and function
Eating disorder
A serious mental health condition involving disordered eating patterns
Body mass index
A height-and-weight screening ratio with known individual limitations
Physical Fitness: Physical fitness
The ability to carry out daily tasks with energy to spare
Cardiorespiratory endurance
The heart and lungs supplying oxygen during sustained activity
Muscular strength
The maximum force a muscle can produce at once
Muscular endurance
A muscle's ability to keep working over time
Flexibility
The range of motion available at a joint
Body composition
The proportion of fat mass to lean mass
Aerobic exercise
Sustained activity using oxygen to fuel movement
Anaerobic exercise
Short intense activity exceeding the oxygen supply
FITT principle
Frequency, intensity, time, and type of exercise
Principle of overload
Improvement requires demanding more than the body is used to
Principle of progression
Increasing demand gradually to avoid injury
Principle of specificity
Training adaptations match the type of training performed
Target heart rate zone
The intensity range producing cardiovascular benefit
Resting heart rate
Beats per minute at rest, a rough fitness indicator
Warm-up and cool-down
Gradual transitions that prepare and recover the body
Sedentary lifestyle
A pattern of prolonged inactivity linked to chronic disease
Mental and Emotional Health: Mental health
Emotional, psychological, and social wellbeing
Self-esteem
How a person values and regards themselves
Resilience
The ability to recover and adapt after difficulty
Emotion
A physiological and psychological response to a situation
Emotional regulation
Managing emotional responses in healthy ways
Anxiety disorder
Persistent excessive worry that interferes with daily life
Depression
A prolonged low mood with loss of interest and function
Warning signs of mental health problems
Withdrawal, mood change, sleep change, and loss of interest
Stigma
Negative labelling that discourages people from seeking help
Counseling
Professional support for emotional and behavioural concerns
Trusted adult
A responsible person a young person can turn to for help
Coping strategy
A healthy method of handling difficulty, such as talking or exercise
Grief
The natural emotional response to significant loss
When to seek help
Any time distress persists or interferes with daily functioning
Stress Management: The body's response to a demand or challenge
The event or condition triggering a stress response
Negative stress that harms performance and health
The rapid physiological reaction to a perceived threat
The hormone driving the immediate stress response
The hormone released during prolonged stress
Long-term stress linked to heart disease and weakened immunity
Headache, muscle tension, fatigue, and disrupted sleep
Organising tasks to reduce avoidable pressure
A technique slowing the heart rate and calming the nervous system
Tensing and releasing muscle groups to reduce tension
Exercise reducing stress hormones and improving mood
Insufficient sleep amplifying stress and impairing judgement
Relationships that buffer the impact of stressful events
Substance Use and Abuse: Drug
Any substance that changes how the body or mind functions
Medicine
A drug used to treat, prevent, or diagnose illness
Over-the-counter drug
A medicine legally sold without a prescription
Prescription drug
A medicine requiring authorisation from a licensed provider
Drug misuse
Taking a medicine in a way other than directed
Drug abuse
Intentional improper use of a substance
Tolerance
Needing more of a substance to achieve the same effect
Dependence
A state in which the body requires a substance to function normally
Addiction
Compulsive use despite harmful consequences
Withdrawal
Physical and mental symptoms when a substance is stopped
Depressant
A drug slowing central nervous system activity, such as alcohol
Stimulant
A drug speeding body functions, such as nicotine or cocaine
Blood alcohol concentration
The percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream
Effects of alcohol on the teenage brain
Interference with development of judgement and memory regions
Nicotine
The highly addictive stimulant in tobacco and most vape products
Vaping risks
Nicotine addiction plus lung injury from inhaled aerosols
Opioid
A powerful pain-relieving drug class with high overdose risk
Naloxone
A medication that can reverse an opioid overdose
Secondhand smoke
Tobacco smoke inhaled involuntarily by nonsmokers
Recovery and treatment
Structured support helping a person stop and stay stopped
Human Body Systems: The heart and vessels transporting blood throughout the body
Vessels carrying blood away from versus back to the heart
The lungs and airways exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide
The tiny air sacs where gas exchange occurs
The organs breaking food into absorbable nutrients
The organ where most nutrient absorption takes place
The brain, spinal cord, and nerves controlling body activity
The cell that transmits nerve signals
The bones providing structure, protection, and blood cell production
The tissues producing movement and maintaining posture
The glands releasing hormones that regulate body processes
The kidneys and related organs removing waste from blood
The maintenance of stable internal conditions
The skin, hair, and nails forming the body's outer barrier
Disease Prevention: An illness caused by a pathogen and able to spread
An illness not caused by a pathogen, such as diabetes
A noncellular pathogen that replicates inside host cells
A single-celled organism, some species of which cause illness
A medicine effective against bacteria but not viruses
Bacteria evolving to survive drugs that once killed them
A preparation training the immune system to recognise a pathogen
Protection of a population when enough members are immune
A regional outbreak versus a worldwide one
A long-lasting condition such as heart disease or asthma
Conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels
A condition where cells respond poorly to insulin
Uncontrolled cell growth that can spread through the body
A trait or behaviour raising the chance of developing a disease
Testing for a disease before symptoms appear
Washing that interrupts one of the most common transmission routes
First Aid and Emergency Care: Immediate care given before professional help arrives
Legal protection for people who reasonably assist in an emergency
Treating all body fluids as potentially infectious
Chest compressions and rescue breaths for cardiac arrest
About 100 to 120 chest compressions per minute
A device that analyses heart rhythm and can deliver a shock
Abdominal thrusts for a conscious person who cannot breathe
Placing an unresponsive breathing person on their side
Applying firm direct pressure with a clean cloth
A life-threatening drop in circulation requiring immediate help
First, second, and third degree by depth of tissue damage
Rest, ice, compression, and elevation for sprains
A brain injury from impact requiring removal from activity
Heavy sweating and weakness versus a medical emergency with hot dry skin
A severe allergic reaction treated with epinephrine
Relationships and Communication: Healthy relationship
One built on respect, trust, honesty, and equality
Unhealthy relationship
One marked by control, disrespect, or isolation
Boundaries
Limits a person sets about what they will accept
Consent
A clear, freely given, reversible agreement
Assertive communication
Expressing needs directly while respecting others
Passive communication
Failing to express needs, often building resentment
Aggressive communication
Expressing needs in a way that disregards others
Active listening
Fully attending and reflecting back what was said
I-statement
Framing a concern around your own feelings rather than blame
Nonverbal communication
Meaning carried by tone, posture, and facial expression
Conflict resolution
Working through disagreement toward a workable outcome
Compromise
Each side adjusting to reach a shared solution
Bullying
Repeated aggressive behaviour involving a power imbalance
Cyberbullying
Bullying carried out through digital platforms
Bystander intervention
Safely acting to interrupt harm rather than watching
Empathy
Understanding and sharing another person's feelings
Consumer Health and Media Literacy: Consumer health
Making informed decisions about health products and services
Media literacy
The ability to critically analyse media messages
Advertising technique
A persuasive strategy such as bandwagon or testimonial
Bandwagon appeal
Suggesting everyone is already using a product
Testimonial
Using a celebrity or user endorsement to sell a product
Health fraud
Selling a product with false or unproven health claims
Dietary supplement
A product that is far less regulated than a medication
Reliable health source
Government, university, or major medical organisation information
Peer-reviewed research
Studies evaluated by independent experts before publication
Anecdotal evidence
A personal story, which cannot establish that a treatment works
Placebo effect
Improvement caused by expectation rather than treatment
Body image and media
Edited images distorting expectations about appearance
Comparison price of care
Evaluating cost and quality before choosing a provider
Patient rights
Entitlements including informed consent and privacy of records
Health insurance basics
Premiums, deductibles, and copays determining what you pay
